software.now: verify reliable; reproduce reliable if a harness exists; edit reliable once the plan is frozen; review and onboard assisted

analyze.trigger: A failing path, stack trace, or error log is present and the owning file is unknown. Quiet when the ask is to edit, run tests, or explain the whole repo.
analyze.doneWhen: Output one record, and a program reads each field: (1) a log line quoted verbatim with its line number in the log file, read back with python3 (line N of the log equals the quote); (2) that line names the entry file, given as file:line from the trace, and the file:line exists in the tree; (3) the broken invariant quoted verbatim from a source line at a stated file:line; (4) a do-not-touch list of paths, each present in `git ls-files`. A log with no matching line is a valid result: write "unmatched" and stop; do not guess a file.
analyze.forbidden: Guessing a file from a noisy log that the grep did not return; naming a file with no quoted line.

reproduce.trigger: A bug report and an existing test harness are present. Quiet when asked to fix it, or when no harness exists.
reproduce.doneWhen: The named smallest command (pytest or python3 -m unittest, one test id, pinned input file) exits non-zero on the unedited tree, and its output is recorded as two quoted lines: the expected value and the actual value, the actual copied verbatim from that run's output (the assertion line) so a program finds it in the output. Red is the pass here. Exit 0 means the bug did not reproduce and the check fails. No harness in the repo is a valid result: report "harness: absent" and stop; status holds as reliable only when a harness exists.
reproduce.forbidden: Editing source to make the failure appear, or reporting a failure that was not run red.

edit.trigger: A frozen plan lists the files to change and any signature change. Quiet when no plan exists or the plan is still open.
edit.doneWhen: `git diff --name-only` lists exactly the files named in the plan and no others (a sorted set comparison of the two lists); `git diff -U0` shows no added or removed `def` or `class` line unless the plan lists that signature change; and each hunk the plan marks non-obvious has an added one-line comment inside that hunk. An empty diff is a valid result when the plan needs no change: report "diff: empty".
edit.forbidden: Drift: editing an unnamed file, renaming a public signature, or tidying beyond the plan.

verify.trigger: A project directory holds verify_gate.sh and a change claims to be finished. Quiet when no gate script exists: report gate absent and stop.
verify.doneWhen: `bash verify_gate.sh` in the project directory exits 0 (unit test, then build, then render-compare against the fixture; the first failure stops it). The Stop hook blocks 'done' until it does. The script runs `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests` (tune fixture tests test_simple and test_zero_numerator in tests/test_mod.py), then py_compile, then cmp against fixture.txt, under one exit code. A non-zero exit is a valid result: report RED with the exit code and the first failing line quoted verbatim, declared_done false. No verify_gate.sh in the directory is also a valid result: report "gate: absent" and stop. Never report GREEN without exit 0.
verify.forbidden: declaring done, or editing any file, on a model read of the output; verify never fixes

migrate.trigger: One transform of one file shape applies to many files. Quiet for a single file, or when two different shapes are mixed.
migrate.doneWhen: `git ls-files` filtered by the one file shape prints N target paths, and the worker manifest lists exactly those N paths (sorted set comparison). N of 0 is a valid result: report "targets: 0".
migrate.forbidden: Guessing the file list instead of enumerating it, or accepting a file whose result was not rechecked.

review.trigger: A diff or pull request is present. Quiet when asked to fix the code or to run tests.
review.doneWhen: Every comment carries file:line and the quoted line text, and the quote appears verbatim at that line in `git diff` output. Any comment with no matching quote is dropped; zero surviving comments is a valid result: report "findings: 0".
review.forbidden: Posting a comment that cannot point at a line, or over-commenting style; cross-file logic no single line shows is reported unsupported, not smoothed.

onboard.trigger: A named request or endpoint and a runtime log are present. Quiet for explain-the-repo or architecture overview asks.
onboard.doneWhen: One record, read by a program: the hops of one request from entry to store, each as file:line of the hop function (the line exists in the file and contains the function name) plus the owning module; the first hop is the route entry and the last hop is the store call. Exactly one hop is also matched to a runtime log line quoted verbatim with its log line number; python3 reading that log line number returns the quote, and the line names the hop's function or file. No log line matching any hop is a valid result: report "log: unmatched" and stop.
onboard.forbidden: Touring the repo: describing modules that are not on the traced request path.

research.now: assisted; deep-research URL hallucination is worse than search-augmented; volume is not reliability

retrieve.trigger: A question or topic needs outside sources: papers, DOIs, preprints, pages. Quiet when the source text is already in context, or when the ask is to extract or synthesize.
retrieve.doneWhen: Every opened identifier (DOI, arXiv id, or URL the scrape tool returned and opened) is listed under "opened" and ends in exactly one place: "kept" or "dropped-recap". Every kept source has its identifier, a quoted title line with its locator (page or line), an access date (YYYY-MM-DD), and a tag "primary" (the publisher, DOI landing, arXiv, or original-document page) or "recap". A "recap" is kept only when the line "no-primary-opened" names the primary identifier that failed to open. A recap that opened while a primary of the same work also opened is not kept: it is listed under "dropped-recap" with the primary identifier that replaced it. Every hit that did not open is listed under "discarded" with the failing identifier. Zero kept sources is a valid result: print "retrieved: 0" and list the discards. Counts must satisfy: kept + dropped-recap = opened.
retrieve.forbidden: Writing an identifier or URL the tool did not return, or keeping a recap when the primary source opened. A hit that does not open is discarded, never repaired by guessing.

extract.trigger: A source page or PDF text is in context and the ask is its stated facts. Quiet when the source is not yet fetched, or when two sources are being compared.
extract.doneWhen: Each extracted item is a verbatim sentence found in the source text at a stated page or line, confirmed by substring match against the pdftotext or page text. Each item that is not verbatim is tagged "paraphrase". An item whose sentence states a number also carries a "unit" field and a "scope" field (the sample or scope the number applies to): each must be a substring of the source text at the stated locator, or the literal "absent" when the source gives none. A number with no unit field or no scope field fails. A source with no matching sentence yields "absent"; zero items is a valid result.
extract.forbidden: Paraphrasing under compression without the paraphrase tag, or giving a number without its unit and sample or scope.

gap.trigger: A draft with claims and a searchable corpus are both present. Quiet when there is no draft, or when the ask is a broad survey.
gap.doneWhen: `python3 fixtures/research-gap/check.py --fixture <dir> --out <out.json> --searchlog <log>` exits 0: the claims table validates, every quote is verbatim in the cited document, and the search log holds at most one search. One search is logged when an unsupported claim exists, and it targets the first unsupported claim only, ending resolution "filled" or "open" (declared open is a valid stop). Zero searches is valid when every claim is supported. Runnable today: fixtures/research-gap/check.py is an existing repo program and the search runs through the registered harness desk/tools/localsearch.py; no new program is needed.
gap.forbidden: searching a second claim; a quote that is not verbatim; marking a cited-but-mismatching claim supported

conflict.trigger: Two or more sources state different things about the same point. Quiet when only one source exists or the sources agree.
conflict.doneWhen: A script reads the side-by-side table and exits 0 only when: two quotes each appear verbatim in their cited source at a stated locator; one line begins "Disagreement:" and one line begins "Decider:" (what evidence would decide it); and the sentence after the quotes contains no number absent from both quotes and none of the blend words "average", "mean of", "midpoint", "between the two", "roughly", "split the difference". Status stays weak: a blended conclusion worded without a number or a listed word still needs a person's read, so the program catches the figure and the wording, not every smoothing.
conflict.forbidden: Averaging the two sources, or writing a blended figure or a midpoint conclusion in the sentence after the quotes.

synthesize.trigger: Extracted, sourced findings exist and a written answer is wanted. Quiet when no sources have been gathered yet.
synthesize.doneWhen: A script splits the answer into sentences and exits 0 only when every sentence carries exactly one source id or the literal label "unsupported" (a sentence with two source ids or two labels is two claims and fails), the first sentence begins "Answer:", every sentence beginning "Conflict:" comes after all non-conflict sentences, and the printed count "claims: N/N sourced-or-labeled" has N equal to the sentence count. An empty answer is valid: "claims: 0/0".
synthesize.forbidden: Keeping a sentence that has neither a source nor the unsupported label, or putting two claims in one sentence.

monitor.trigger: A prior memo exists as a file with a date and a half-life in days on each claim. Quiet when there is no memo file, because there is nothing to diff.
monitor.doneWhen: Two readings must agree. Clock: a python3 date computation (claim date plus half-life days against today, never a model's judgment) prints the expired claim ids; every printed id has an added line marked "expired" and no unprinted id has one. Diff: `git diff --numstat` of the memo file reports 0 deleted lines, so the old conclusion stays visible and a changed conclusion appears as an added line marked "changed" beneath it; every source id on an added line is absent from the memo at HEAD (`git show HEAD:<memo>`), so only new sources were added. No new sources and no expiries is a valid result: an empty diff.
monitor.forbidden: Deciding by model judgment that a claim has expired or is still fresh, or rewriting the memo whole so the old conclusion disappears.

scientific.now: Robin-style loop is real; the model does not run the wet lab

triage.trigger: A candidate list (papers, records, datasets) and a written inclusion rule file are both present. Quiet when the rule is only in someone's head, or for deep reading.
triage.doneWhen: A program reads the rule file and triage table: every row is included, excluded, or unread; each included row cites the rule id that admits it and each excluded row cites the rule id that excludes it, a row with no rule id fails; included count is at most the cap; included + excluded + unread equals the candidate total; unread ids are listed. Empty included set with unread rows is a valid result.
triage.forbidden: Including a paper because it is interesting when no rule id admits it; excluding by vibe with no rule id; silently dropping what was not read instead of recording it as unread.

hypothesis.trigger: A research question or literature gap is stated and a hypothesis is wanted. Quiet for protocol steps (design) or when a result file is the input (update).
hypothesis.doneWhen: jq -e over the hypothesis record passes: non-empty measurement, direction (increase, decrease, no-change), and control; or the record carries status rejected-not-runnable with a reason, which is a valid result. A missing field with no rejection status fails.
hypothesis.forbidden: Keeping a hypothesis that cannot be run (vague measurement, no direction, or no control) as runnable instead of rejecting it.

design.trigger: An accepted hypothesis record and a list of materials the lab already has are present. Quiet when asked to run the protocol or start an instrument.
design.doneWhen: Only a scientist can accept the plan: the draft lists materials on hand, ordered steps, and the single failure that would kill the idea, then stops at awaiting scientist acceptance. No program passes it.
design.forbidden: Treating the draft as accepted, starting hardware, or listing a material the lab does not have as if it were on hand.
design.gate: ABSENT hardware-start, accept (prepare the plan, stop; a scientist accepts and a person starts any instrument)

analyze.trigger: Raw tabular or sequencing data files are present and a result is wanted. Quiet for proprietary instrument dumps no script can read: report unsupported.
analyze.doneWhen: The verifier, not the script's author, reruns the analysis script in a clean directory with only the raw files; exit code 0 passes. Non-zero, missing script, or skipped rerun means nothing is claimed; unsupported input is a valid result.
analyze.forbidden: Reporting a number or figure the script did not produce, or hiding single-outlier dependence: if dropping one point flips the result, say so.

update.trigger: An old hypothesis record and a result file are both present. Quiet when no result file exists or a new hypothesis from scratch is wanted.
update.doneWhen: One program over the update record, old hypothesis record, and result file passes only if every cited quote equals the text at its file:line locator, every old branch id is in exactly one of dropped or kept, every dropped branch points at a cited quote, and proposed next measurements number at most 1. No change forced (nothing dropped, zero measurements) is a valid result.
update.forbidden: Keeping a dead branch because it was the old one, citing a result not in the file, or proposing more than the next measurement.

manuscript.trigger: Result files and a figure exist and a draft is wanted. Quiet when no result files exist or when the ask is a verdict on the claim.
manuscript.doneWhen: One program scans the single draft file, body and self-review alike, and flags each line holding a number with no file:line locator in a result file or a verdict or settled-claim word, and flags a self-review section whose heading lacks the word DRAFT; it passes when it flags zero lines. A draft with no self-review or an empty draft for empty results is valid.
manuscript.forbidden: Upgrading the draft self-review into a verdict, or stating a claim as settled; the human owns the claim.

transcribe.trigger: A named method and its source text are present and the ask is to copy the steps; quiet without the source or for graph, repair, campaign, run.
transcribe.doneWhen: Every step carries a verbatim source quote with page/line or step locator, matched by program; quantities and units appear in the quote; each skipped step is written as GAP; zero-step or unread source is a valid result.
transcribe.forbidden: Inventing a step the source skips instead of marking a GAP; rewriting units or quantities.

graph.trigger: Transcribed steps and a graph schema are present and the ask is a graph; quiet when no schema is supplied.
graph.doneWhen: jq -e filter encoding the supplied schema's required node fields (id, action, params object, source step locator) and edge fields (from and to each equal an existing node id, handoff names the material or output passed) exits 0 over the graph file, exit code quoted; every edge without a handoff field or with a dangling id fails; one node per instrument action with parameters as node fields; GAP stays a GAP field; empty step list gives an empty graph and empty edge list that exits 0.
graph.forbidden: Fake edges: linking adjacent nodes without a real handoff, or putting parameters in prose.

repair.trigger: A graph and validator output naming a failing node are present; quiet when no node is named.
repair.doneWhen: Validator re-run on the repaired graph: diff of validator output before vs after (git diff --no-index, output quoted) shows the named node's error line removed and zero added error lines, and the re-run exit code is quoted; clean graph with empty diff is valid.
repair.forbidden: Restyling the rest of the graph: reordering keys, renaming nodes, reformatting, or touching an unnamed node.

campaign.trigger: A validated graph and a goal for repeated runs are present; the skill prepares the plan and stops.
campaign.doneWhen: jq -e filter over the campaign file exits 0, exit code quoted: every parameter has min and max set before the loop, a stop condition field is non-empty, the iteration log schema has the required fields and zero entries; grep -c '^STARTED-BY:$' prints 1 (line blank until a person writes it); a person starting the hardware is the gate, not part of this check.
campaign.forbidden: Starting or simulating-as-real a hardware run, or writing a loop with no bound or stop condition.
campaign.gate: ABSENT hardware-start, instrument control (prepare bounds, stop, and log; a person starts the hardware)

handoff.trigger: A graph file and an editor-format target, or a manually edited copy to resync, are present; quiet without an editor format.
handoff.doneWhen: Diff of the jq node projection (id, action, params) of the resynced graph file and of the editor-format file against the expected projection (pre-edit graph with only the person's edits applied) is empty for both views, differing nodes: 0, count quoted; edited values appear; no manual edit gives an empty diff.
handoff.forbidden: Rewriting untouched nodes on resync: regenerating the graph, renumbering ids, or reordering nodes.

data.now: profile and one-field clean reliable; define gated

profile.trigger: A csv, table or extract is present and the ask is to know its shape. Quiet when the ask is to fix values, chart, or answer a business question.
profile.doneWhen: `python3` over the file prints rows, per-column null count, per-column type, the grain (the column set unique per row, or "none"), and one line "id-as-measure: <col>" for each id column used as a measure, then writes profile.json with keys rows, columns (null count and type each), grain, id_as_measure. Check: a second python3 recount of the file must equal profile.json on rows, on every per-column null count, on grain (distinct tuples of the grain columns equal rows, or grain is "none"), and the number of "id-as-measure:" lines equals the length of id_as_measure; any mismatch is a nonzero count of differences. An empty file is a valid result: rows 0, grain "none".
profile.forbidden: Stating a count, null total or grain from reading a sample instead of tool output, or summing a numeric id column as if it were a measure.

clean.trigger: One named column and one named rule (trim, cast, dedupe, null-fill, drop). Quiet when the ask names several fields or says clean the data with no field; ask for one field.
clean.doneWhen: `python3` applies the one rule and prints "rows before: N", "rows after: M", "dropped: K", and writes dropped.csv holding all K dropped rows. Check: N = M + K, where K equals the data-row count of dropped.csv. K = 0 with an empty dropped.csv is a valid result.
clean.forbidden: Cleaning a second field in the same directive (the loose-directive failure), or deleting dropped rows instead of keeping them queryable.

hypothesis.trigger: A question of the form compare A to B over a slice. Quiet when a chart is requested before the query exists; write the query first.
hypothesis.doneWhen: A file hypothesis.md holds a line "comparison: ...", a line "slice: ..." and a fenced saved query. Check: one `python3` run of that saved query exits 0, and the directory listing before and after the directive differs only by hypothesis.md (no png, svg or chart html added). An empty result set is valid: report "rows: 0".
hypothesis.forbidden: Jumping to a chart (adding a png, svg or chart html) before the query is saved, or writing a comparison with no slice.

chart.trigger: A saved query and its result are present and a chart is asked for. Quiet when the query is missing or the ask adds extra series.
chart.doneWhen: The chart spec (json or svg source) names the query file as its data source. Check: one `python3` run over the spec quotes, each with file and line, the title (which must contain the hypothesis.md "comparison:" text), the series count (must be 1 unless the ask said otherwise), and one labeled value that equals the same value quoted from the query result; any inequality exits nonzero.
chart.forbidden: Adding a decorative second series (the spec must keep exactly one series unless the ask said otherwise), a title that does not name the saved comparison line, or plotting values not taken from the saved query result.
absentTools: chart-spec validator (only Bash:playwright screenshot is registered)

anomaly.trigger: A metric spike, dip or odd value with a data file or query. Quiet when the ask is why it happened; isolate first.
anomaly.doneWhen: `python3` filters the slice, recomputes the metric on it, and prints "anomaly: <row id or date>" with the recomputed value and the original value. Check: slice row count is above 0 and both values are printed, or the output says "anomaly: none" and exits 0.
anomaly.forbidden: Offering a cause story before the slice has rerun (a rule for the writer; the count check does not read it).

reconcile.trigger: Two extracts and one written metric definition are present. Quiet when only one extract exists (report unsupported) or when the ask is for the number.
reconcile.doneWhen: `python3` applies the written definition to both extracts and prints "total A: x", "total B: y", "unmatched keys: n" followed by each key with its source. Check: both totals printed, n equals the listed keys, and no averaged figure appears. Zero unmatched keys is valid; a missing extract is reported "unsupported" and exits 0.
reconcile.forbidden: Averaging the two totals into one number, or reconciling with no written metric definition.

define.trigger: A new or disputed metric. Quiet when a signed definition exists; use it. Draft only, then stop.
define.doneWhen: A file definition.md holds "formula:", "grain:" and "exclusion:" lines and a "signed-by:" line left empty by the model. Check: a person's name on the signed-by line must exist before any query on the metric runs; absent that, queries are refused. The model never fills the signature.
define.forbidden: Filling the signed-by line, or running queries on the metric before a person signs.
define.gate: ABSENT sign (draft formula, grain and exclusion, then stop; a person signs before anyone queries)

print.doneWhen: `python3 fixtures/markets-print/check.py --fixture <dir> --out <out.json>` exits 0: eps, guidance, and surprise each carry a verbatim quote and the line number of the release; every number in the output appears in the release and none comes from the recap only. The check program fixtures/markets-print/check.py already exists in the repo and runs under the registered Bash:python3 with no new program.

filing.trigger: A filing document (text or PDF) is present and the ask is a quoted line with its location. Quiet when only a news recap exists, or the ask is a summary or a trade.
filing.doneWhen: Each claim is one verbatim line from the filing text plus its page or item locator (for example "Item 7, p. 31"). A program extracts the text per page (pdftotext, pages split on form feed) or per item (text between an "Item N" heading and the next one), then greps the quote inside the stated page or item only. The run passes only if every quote is found at its own stated locator; a quote found elsewhere, or a locator that does not exist, fails. A figure that cannot be placed is listed as "skipped" and is a valid result. Zero claims placed is a valid result.
