cross.trigger: Both a filing and a news source are present for one claim. Quiet when only one source exists, or the ask is a merged narrative.
cross.doneWhen: Output has two verbatim quotes per claim, one labelled filing with page or item, one labelled news with its source, and a verdict of agree, disagree, or unplaced. A program confirms each quote appears in its own source; the run passes only if all do. A claim with no filing line is marked "unplaced", which is a valid result.
cross.forbidden: Merging the filing and the news into one voice, or smoothing a disagreement into a single number.
absentTools: EDGAR full-text and XBRL table connector

memo.trigger: Sourced facts exist and the ask is a thesis memo. Quiet when the ask is to buy, sell, or size a position.
memo.doneWhen: A person reads the kill condition line and confirms it is an observable: it names a metric, a threshold, and a date. That is the one check; no program can judge observability. Not part of the check, but required of the draft: one stated thesis, every line tagged fact or inference, and no order and no size.
memo.forbidden: Writing a kill condition that cannot be observed (for example "if sentiment turns"), or adding an order or a size.
memo.gate: ABSENT broker, order (prepare the thesis and kill condition, stop; a person places any order or size)

monitor.trigger: A previous card file and new material both exist. Quiet when there is no prior card.
monitor.doneWhen: `git diff --no-index --unified=0 <old card> <new card>` is parsed by a program against the card format: claim lines read "claim | expires YYYY-MM-DD | text", the kill condition is one line starting "KILL:", added lines start "DELTA ". Pass only if every added line starts "DELTA ", every removed line carries an expires date earlier than the clock date, and no "KILL:" line is removed or changed (new card still holds the old KILL: line byte-equal). A removed line that is not expired, or a rewritten card, fails. An empty diff is a valid result: the card is unchanged.
monitor.forbidden: Rewriting the whole card, keeping a stale claim, or dropping the kill condition.

scenario.trigger: A baseline input set and a named variable to move. Quiet when two variables are named, or when the ask is to place risk.
scenario.doneWhen: A diff of baseline inputs versus scenario inputs shows exactly one changed key, the named variable; all other keys are byte-equal. Two or more changed keys fails. Not part of the check, but required of the output: the thesis shown under that move, then stop. A move that leaves the thesis unchanged is a valid result.
scenario.forbidden: Moving two variables, or continuing past the one requested variable. No order, no size.
scenario.gate: ABSENT broker, order (show the thesis under one move, stop; a person places any order or size)

legal.now: authority weak; all-pass verified legal research is well under reliable; signature gated

extract.trigger: A contract file and one named clause type (for example indemnity or termination) are present. Quiet when no clause type is named, or when the ask is risk, compare, or edits.
extract.doneWhen: Each result row has a verbatim quote that is a substring of the source text and a section locator (section number, page, line). An empty result is valid: print "clause: none found in <sections searched>" and pass. One clause type per pass; a second type is a second pass.
extract.forbidden: Paraphrasing instead of quoting, or filling an empty result with a near clause. Write "none found" instead.

risk.trigger: A contract, one named party, and a written severity rule are present. The scoring party is the one the ask named, fixed for the whole pass (a second party is a second pass). Quiet when no party or no rule is given.
risk.doneWhen: Each score row carries the written rule it applied, a severity from that rule, and a verbatim quote that is a substring of the source with a section locator. A row without a quote is dropped and printed as "unscored: <text>". Zero scored rows is valid.
risk.forbidden: Scoring unquoted text, or scoring from both parties' views at once.
risk.gate: ABSENT sign (prepare the scored sheet and stop; a lawyer signs before anyone relies on it)

compare.trigger: A counterparty draft and a house paper are both present. Quiet when either is missing.
compare.doneWhen: The house paper clause list is the denominator. Each house clause yields exactly one row with status matched, changed, or missing; no row reads "fine" for silence. Output prints "rows: N; missing: M; changed: C; matched: K" with N equal to M+C+K and equal to the house clause count.
compare.forbidden: Treating a missing clause as fine, or dropping a row because the draft is silent.

draft.trigger: A flag naming one clause (flag id, section) and the original text are present. Quiet when no flag exists.
draft.doneWhen: The proposal is a tracked edit of the source. Reverting every tracked edit reproduces the source text byte for byte (original stays visible). Every edit hunk carries the flag id from the ask, and every changed line falls inside the flagged section's line range. A changed line outside the range, an untagged hunk, a hunk tagged with another flag id, or a revert that differs from the source fails. Zero edits is valid when the flag needs none.
draft.forbidden: Rewriting the deal: editing any clause the flag did not name.
draft.gate: ABSENT sign (prepare the flagged-clause edit and stop; a lawyer signs)

authority.trigger: A cite and the proposition it supports are present. Quiet when no cite or proposition is given.
authority.doneWhen: Each cite is resolved: it opens at a source, and the cite string (reporter cite, docket, or statute number) is a substring of the opened text, so the opened page is the cited authority. A quoted holding line with a page or paragraph locator must be a substring of that opened text. A candidate cite that does not open is dropped and printed "dropped: <cite>". Any cite kept or asserted in the output that did not open or resolve (invented), any quoted line not a substring of the opened text, or any pin locator that does not exist fails the card. Zero surviving cites is valid.
authority.forbidden: Keeping a cite that was not opened, or inventing a pin cite or holding quote.

diligence.trigger: A data room or document list and a stated scope are present. Quiet when scope is not stated.
diligence.doneWhen: Two lists print by document name, one per line: in-scope documents and not-read documents. A summary line "in scope: N; read: R; not read: U" prints with N equal to the number of in-scope names listed and equal to R plus U. A document with no read record is listed not-read, never implied-read. One sheet holds the issues: each row has a unique issue id and exactly one issue; every row's document name is in the read set (a not-read document has no row), and the printed row count equals the number of distinct issue ids.
diligence.forbidden: Implying a document was read because it sits in scope.
diligence.gate: ABSENT sign (prepare the coverage sheet and stop; a lawyer signs before anyone relies on it)

design-systems.now: reliable only if the tool rejects; prompt-only lists leak

tokens.trigger: A token source file or design-file link is present and the ask is to style output with the system's values. Quiet when no source file exists: report "unsupported", do not guess values.
tokens.doneWhen: A program reads the source file and, for each token name used in the output, prints the name, its source locator (file path and line, or Figma variable name from get_variable_defs) and the value the source states. It exits non-zero and lists by name any token absent from the source, any token whose value in the output differs from the source value, and any raw hex or literal spacing value in the output where a token name belongs. An empty token set is a valid result: report "absent", never invent.
tokens.forbidden: Sampling a hex or spacing value from a screenshot instead of reading the source file, or writing the hex where the token name belongs.

ban-list.trigger: A named ban list exists, shorter than the design system, and output must pass it. Quiet when asked to ban taste or style opinions; those are not testable.
ban-list.doneWhen: `pytest` over the ban-list test file exits 0 on the output: one test per banned pattern. Any hit exits non-zero and names the pattern. A banned pattern with no test is not on the list. An empty ban list is a valid result: report "no bans", exit 0.
ban-list.forbidden: Enforcing the ban list by instruction in the prompt, or banning taste, so the fail is a plea rather than a test.

components.trigger: A component list exists and output is built from components. Quiet when no list is supplied: report "unsupported".
components.doneWhen: `python3` over the output prints "unlisted: N" and a record line "component: <name>" for each use; exit 0 only when N is 0. Any raw substitute (an element or markup standing in for a listed component) counts as unlisted and fails. An output using no components is a valid result: "unlisted: 0, used: 0".
components.forbidden: Keeping the component list only in the prompt, so a raw substitute leaks through; the list must be what the tool exposes.

flows.trigger: One page type and its one template screenshot exist. A request naming two page types is two directives: pick one and diff against that template only. Quiet when no template exists.
flows.doneWhen: A real screenshot of the output (npx playwright screenshot) is diffed against the one named template screenshot; the diff reports "off-template regions: 0". Spacing and type are held to the template: the template renders token spacing and type, so any deviation in either appears as an off-template region. Any off-template region fails, listed by locator. No rendered page is a valid result: "unread", not a pass.
flows.forbidden: Judging a region on-template by looking at it instead of the diff, or waving through an off-template region.

cli.trigger: A brand rejecting CLI is named or present. A markdown guide is not this directive. Quiet when no CLI exists: report "tool absent", do not substitute a model.
cli.doneWhen: The brand CLI exits 0 on on-system output; on off-system output it exits non-zero and prints the failed rule id. Never "almost" pass. The CLI is absent in this environment: report "tool absent", the check is not runnable, and no script or model stands in for the reject. With the CLI absent, no pass is possible; the result is "tool absent".
cli.forbidden: Rejecting off-system output in a plea or review comment instead of the tool, or treating a near-pass as a pass.

motion-games-3d.now: assisted; tool success is not scene success; max effort only on opening seconds

still.trigger: A request for a single frame with one named subject, to be scored. Quiet when the ask is to animate, render a sequence, or touch a level or engine project.
still.doneWhen: jq -e '(.frames|length)==1 and (.subject|type=="string") and (.score|type=="number")' still.json exits 0; score null with no scorer is reported unscored, a valid result; a human score is assisted, never a pass.
still.forbidden: Animating, or adding a second subject or second frame, before the still is scored; writing a score the scorer did not return.

time.trigger: A time t and a renderer that takes t as its only time input. Quiet when no t-addressable renderer exists (generic video generator) or when the ask is a full render.
time.doneWhen: Render the frame at t into an empty out/ directory as frame_t.png; one program exits 0 only if out/ holds exactly one file (frame_t.png, count 1, so no full render and no other frame) and cmp out/frame_t.png expected_t.png exits 0, where expected_t.png is the brief's reference frame for that t; no reference frame means unchecked, and a renderer that is not a function of t is reported unsupported, both valid results.
time.forbidden: Rendering the full sequence to reach frame t, or drawing any frame other than t (a second frame file in the output directory is the failure).

score.trigger: A contact sheet with a per-frame score file from an external scorer. Quiet when no external score exists, or when the ask is the full render.
score.doneWhen: A program over before.json and after.json prints 'changed frames: 1' (only the worst-scoring frame's entry differs); below threshold is a valid result and no full render starts.
score.forbidden: Fixing more than the worst frame, or starting the full render before the threshold is met (a rescore that does not rise is reported, not hidden).

asset.trigger: A request to make or fix a mesh, UV, or rig asset. Quiet when the ask is to place the asset in a level or to bundle all stages in one prompt.
asset.doneWhen: jq -e '(["mesh","uv","rig","animation"] as $o | .stages==$o[:(.stages|length)]) and (.imported==false) and (.placed_in_level==false) and (if (.stages|index("animation")) then (.rig.kind=="default") and (.animation.count==1) and (.animation.played_on=="default") else true end)' asset.json exits 0; a manifest of only completed earlier stages is valid; editor playback stays assisted.
asset.forbidden: Bundling mesh, UV, rig and animation in one prompt, or importing or placing the asset in the level before one animation played on the default rig.

level.trigger: A level edit in exactly one change class: terrain, light, character, or interaction. Quiet when the ask spans classes or wants unattended level building.
level.doneWhen: A program reads level_classes.json (change class to its file globs) and the output of git diff --name-only, and exits 0 only if every changed path matches the named class's globs and none match another class's; a path in two classes or none is reported 'class not separable', and an empty diff after a revert is valid; the editor check is quoted separately and no editor check means unvalidated.
level.forbidden: Treating tool success as scene success: calling the level done because the edit command exited 0, or changing a second class in the same pass.

engine.trigger: An engine project (Unity, Unreal, Godot) on disk and a request to change one system. Quiet when no project is present or the system is unnamed.
engine.doneWhen: A program reads systems.json (system name to its file globs), read.json (the pre-edit quote: system path and line, recorded before the first edit) and the output of git diff --name-only, and exits 0 only if the quoted path matches the named system's globs, the quote is non-empty, and every changed path matches the named system's globs; the path walk is reported 'not run' because the connector is absent.
engine.forbidden: Writing before reading the project (no quoted system path and line before the first edit), or editing a system that was not named first.

audio.now: ceiling closed; names reliable only if the list is a tool

cut.trigger: One take file and one region with start and end times; quiet for episode-wide restitch or reorder.
cut.doneWhen: python3 diff script exits 0 printing 'outside-region: N/N samples unchanged'; a no-op cut is valid.
cut.forbidden: Restitching the episode: changing, moving, or re-joining anything outside the named region.

names.trigger: A script or transcript and a pronunciation list file are present; no list means report no list and stop.
names.doneWhen: python3 script loads the pronunciation list file itself and exits 0 whenever the list was read, printing 'missing: <name> line <n>' for each proper noun not on the list (a flag is a valid result, not a failure) and 'names: K/N listed'; empty script prints 'names: 0/0'; exits non-zero only if the list file is unreadable.
names.forbidden: Guessing a pronunciation or spelling for a proper noun not on the list instead of flagging it.

score.trigger: A rule file and existing music assets are present; quiet when asked to compose a new theme.
score.doneWhen: python3 script exits 0 only if the hook cue lies inside its rule window using a rule-named asset, printing 'hook: ok'; unplaced hook prints 'hook: absent' and is valid.
score.forbidden: Composing or generating a new theme to fill the hook, or placing a cue the rule file does not name.

assemble.trigger: An approved-takes list and take files are present; quiet when a take is unapproved or audio regeneration is asked.
assemble.doneWhen: python3 script hashes takes and exits 0 only if exactly the approved takes appear in listed order with unchanged hashes, printing 'assembled: N/N takes'; empty list valid.
assemble.forbidden: Regenerating or re-recording audio to fill a gap or substituting an unapproved take.
assemble.gate: ABSENT accept (prepare the ordered take list and hash report, stop; a person listens and accepts the assembly)

writing.now: outline reliable; draft assisted; cut can be a claim-count diff

outline.trigger: A topic or source notes are present and no outline exists. Quiet when an outline file is given and the ask is prose, or when the ask is to shorten or fact-check.
outline.doneWhen: `python3` over the outline file exits 0 and prints "claims: N/N slotted": N claim lines, each with a unique order slot, and zero prose lines (a line that is neither a numbered claim nor blank). A claim with no slot is cut, not kept. An empty outline ("claims: 0/0") is a valid result when the source holds no claim.
outline.forbidden: Writing prose or a transition sentence in the outline, or keeping a claim that has no slot.

draft.trigger: An outline file with claim ids and a voice file are both present. Quiet when only one exists, or when the ask is cutting, channel change, or fact-checking.
draft.doneWhen: `python3` over the draft and the outline exits 0 and prints "violations: 0": one check, claim-to-paragraph mapping against the outline file. violations = paragraphs carrying zero or more than one outline id tag (a paragraph with two claims or an untagged paragraph) + tags that are not outline ids (an unmapped paragraph is a new claim) + outline ids used more than once + outline ids missing from the draft. A new claim hidden inside a correctly tagged paragraph is not detectable by program, and the voice file (bans, style) is not measured here: both stay a human read. A missing voice file is a valid result: stop and report "voice file absent".
draft.forbidden: Adding a claim that is not in the outline, to fill a paragraph or smooth a transition.

cut.trigger: A finished piece is present with a length target. Quiet when the ask is new material, a restyle, or a channel change.
cut.doneWhen: `python3` over the original and the cut exits 0 only when words fell and nothing was inserted: cut words < original words, and the cut's tokens are an ordered subsequence of the original's (a diff shows only deletions), so no new claim can be swapped in at equal count and no restyle passes. It prints "claims: A -> B; words: X -> Y; inserted: 0" with B <= A. Equal claim counts are a valid result. A cut that rewords to shorten fails and goes to a person.
cut.forbidden: Adding a claim while shortening, or restyling the piece into a new one.

variant.trigger: A source piece, a frozen fact list with an "offer:" line, and a target channel are present. Quiet when no fact list exists or when the ask is to change the offer or numbers.
variant.doneWhen: `python3` over the fact list (one item per line, the offer on a line starting "offer:", then numbers and names), the source piece, and the variant exits 0 and prints "violations: 0": one check, frozen facts. violations = fact-list items not verbatim in the variant (the offer text is an item, so a dropped offer counts) + a non-empty fact list with no "offer:" line + digit-bearing tokens in the variant found in neither the source piece nor the fact list (an added number). A missing item exits non-zero and names the line. An empty fact list prints "facts: 0/0" and is valid. An added non-numeric fact is not detectable by program, and the voice file (bans, style) is not measured here: both stay a human read.
variant.forbidden: Changing a number, dropping the offer, or adding a fact while adapting to the channel.

series.trigger: A brand file and a previous piece are present. Quiet when no brand file exists; session chat is never the memory.
series.doneWhen: `cmp` over two files exits 0: bans.expected (the ban lines read from the brand file's "Bans" heading) and bans.kept (the same lines minus any whose phrase occurs in the new piece, so a piece that restates a ban also drops it). Exit 1 names the first differing line. One check: the new piece keeps the brand file's bans. The previous piece is context for voice, not a second measured check. A missing brand file is a valid result: stop and report "brand file absent".
series.forbidden: Taking rules from session chat instead of the brand file, or restating the rules inside the draft (a restated ban phrase also fails cmp).

fact.trigger: A piece with factual claims is present. Quiet when the piece holds no checkable claim or the ask is style.
fact.doneWhen: `python3` over the piece and the source corpus exits 0 and prints "claims: N = S sourced + U unsupported" with N equal to the claim count. A claim line ends with exactly one of: the label "unsupported", or a quote plus locator (doc, line) whose quote appears verbatim at that line of that source (localsearch finds it; the program compares the text). A quote absent from the cited line, a missing locator, or any other label ("likely", "reportedly") exits non-zero naming the claim line. Zero sourced is a valid result.
fact.forbidden: Upgrading a label by tone: a hedged or confident claim passed off as sourced without a matching quote, or a third state such as "likely".

sales.now: assisted; useful mechanism is clustering and question generation; send and spend denied

frame.trigger: An offer or market note is present and candidate frames (buyer, job, what they pay for) are asked for.
frame.doneWhen: Write frames to frames.json as a list of {buyer, job, pays_for}. `jq -e 'all(.[]; (.buyer|length>0) and (.job|length>0) and (.pays_for|length>0))' frames.json` exits 0. Any frame with an empty buyer is deleted, and the dropped count is printed. An empty list `[]` is a valid result when no buyer can be named.
frame.forbidden: Keeping a frame whose buyer is blank, generic, or implied.

cluster.trigger: A file of raw customer or interview quotes is present and grouping is asked for.
cluster.doneWhen: Write clusters.json as {group: [{quote, source, line}]}. A python3 script reads quotes.txt and exits 0 only if every group holds at least one quote that appears verbatim in quotes.txt at the cited line. It prints "groups: N, quoted: N/N". Zero quotes in, zero groups out: it prints "groups: 0, quoted: 0/0" and exits 0.
cluster.forbidden: Inventing a segment that no quote supports, or paraphrasing a quote to pass the match.

question.trigger: A stated sales gap needs falsifiable explanatory questions.
question.doneWhen: Write questions.json as a list of {question, refuted_if}. `jq -e 'all(.[]; (.question|endswith("?")) and (.refuted_if|length>0) and (has("answer")|not))' questions.json` exits 0. An empty list is valid when no gap is stated.
question.forbidden: Answering the question in the same directive.

brief.trigger: A named prospect and an upcoming meeting need a pre-call brief from public facts.
brief.doneWhen: Every fact line in brief.md is either quoted or marked unsupported. A quoted fact line carries a verbatim quote and public URL fetched by firecrawl_scrape; an unsupported fact line carries the word "unsupported", no quote, and no number. A python3 script reads brief.md and exits 0 only if every quoted fact's quote is found in the saved page text (a quote not found exits 1), no digit appears outside a quoted span except on the one "prepared:" and one "meeting:" line (each an ISO date YYYY-MM-DD, prepared earlier than meeting), and exactly one line starts "objection:" with non-empty text. It prints "facts: N, quoted: Q, unsupported: U, objection: 1, prepared: before" with Q+U=N. Unsupported facts count as a result and do not fail the check; "no public facts found" (N=0) is a valid result (objection and dates still required).
brief.forbidden: Inventing metrics with no quoted public source.

asset.trigger: A winning frame is recorded and one asset for it is asked for.
asset.doneWhen: `python3 -c` over asset.md counts lines and exits 0 only if exactly one line starts "frame:" and its id equals the winning id in state, exactly one line starts "segment:" and equals the segment named in brief.md, and exactly one line starts "objection:" and equals the objection line in brief.md. It prints "frames: 1/1, segment: 1/1, objection: 1/1". With no winning frame it prints "frames: 0/0" and exits 0; no asset is written.
asset.forbidden: Producing the other frames alongside the winner.

test.trigger: A frame and a budget or audience are present and a smallest test plan is asked for.
test.doneWhen: Write test.json with {frame, smallest_action, cap, kill_result, gate}. `jq -e '(.smallest_action|length>0) and (.cap|length>0) and (.kill_result|length>0) and (.gate|length>0)' test.json` exits 0. Nothing is sent or spent; the plan stops at the gate.
test.forbidden: Opening the gate: sending or committing spend because the plan is ready.
test.gate: ABSENT send, pay (prepare the test sheet with smallest spend and kill result, stop; a person sends or spends)

support.now: classify and exception reliable as code; resolve inside a typed tool; refund, cancel, delete gated

classify.trigger: A ticket text and a policy id list are both present. Quiet when the ask is to reply, resolve, or promise anything.
classify.doneWhen: `python3` lookup exits 0 only if the assigned policy id exists in the policy id list and the quoted policy line matches that entry verbatim, reported as `policy-id: <id> line: <file>:<n>`. The result `escalate: no policy id fits` with exit 0 is valid. An id that does not resolve exits non-zero.
classify.forbidden: Inventing or paraphrasing a policy id or policy line that is not in the id list. If no id fits, escalate.

draft.trigger: A classified intent with policy id and policy line is present. Quiet when no classification exists or the ask is to grant a refund or exception.
draft.doneWhen: `python3` quote check exits 0 only if the draft contains the classified policy line verbatim, matching the entry at the cited `<file>:<n>`; it prints `quoted: <policy-id> line <n>`. A draft that cannot quote its line is not a pass; the result is `unsupported`. This is the only check. Promise creep and intent drift are not checked by it; a person reviews them, which is why status stays assisted. The check program is not written yet, so checkRunnable is false.
draft.forbidden: Promise creep: the draft says or implies a refund, credit, waiver, or exception the policy line does not grant.

known-path.trigger: A workflow definition with ordered steps and a matching ticket are present. Quiet when no workflow matches; that goes to exception.
known-path.doneWhen: `jq -e --slurpfile e expected_state.json '. == $e[0]' state.json` exits 0 and prints `true`. Both files are supplied as input: expected_state.json lists the workflow's ordered steps with their end state, state.json is the observed snapshot, so reordering, skipping, or adding a step makes the arrays unequal. Any variance exits non-zero and routes to support-exception; the agent does not improvise. No model is in the loop, so reliable holds. Fetching a live snapshot needs an absent state reader.
known-path.forbidden: Improvising: adding, skipping, or reordering a step, or repairing a variance instead of handing it to exception.

exception.trigger: A known path step failed or a variance was reported. Quiet when state matches the workflow.
exception.doneWhen: `jq -e --slurpfile f failed_state.json --slurpfile c state.json '(keys-["failed_step","observed","expected","handoff_owner","stopped"]|length==0) and (.failed_step|type=="string" and length>0) and (.handoff_owner|type=="string" and length>0) and (.stopped==true) and (.expected|length>0) and (.observed==$f[0]) and (.observed!=.expected) and ($c[0]==$f[0])' record.json` exits 0 only if the record has exactly the allowed keys (a remedy or any other extra field fails), names the failed step and handoff owner, carries observed equal to the failure-time snapshot, differs from expected, and the current state still equals that snapshot, so no fix was tried outside the record. Otherwise exits non-zero. The stop is this code check, not a model judgment. Stop is the valid result.
exception.forbidden: Guessing a remedy: proposing, trying, or applying a fix after the failure instead of stopping.

resolve.trigger: A classified ticket with an approved path needs a resolution call prepared. Refund, cancel, and delete requests stop here for a person.
resolve.doneWhen: The prepared request sheet validates against its typed schema: it names the typed tool, carries a non-empty idempotency key, and either its action is a non-gated typed action, or its action is refund, cancel, or delete and the sheet has state `awaiting-person` with no executed field. Waiting for a person is the valid result for those three actions. The execution itself is not performed by this skill.
resolve.forbidden: Executing or promising a refund, cancel, or delete, or calling an untyped tool without an idempotency key.
resolve.gate: ABSENT refund, cancel, delete, typed resolution tool (prepare the request sheet with idempotency key, stop; a person executes)

incident.trigger: Log files or log lines are present and a timeline is asked for. Quiet when no logs exist.
incident.doneWhen: `python3` check exits 0 only if every timeline event has `<file>:<line>`, `ts`, and `quote`; the quote equals the line at that locator; the `ts` equals the timestamp parsed from that line; and the events are in non-decreasing `ts` order (ties keep `<file>:<line>` order). An event with no matching log line fails, so no gap is filled; a mis-ordered timeline fails. An empty log yields `events: 0` and exits 0.
incident.forbidden: Filling a gap with a likely story: stating a cause or event no log line supports.

recruiting.now: assisted; decide stops; no hire tool

scorecard.trigger: A job requisition text is present and the ask is to turn it into scorecard lines. Quiet when no req exists, or when the ask concerns a candidate.
scorecard.doneWhen: Every scorecard line carries a verbatim quote from the req with its line number, and a program confirms each quote is a substring of the req at that line (python3 exits 0, prints "lines: N/N quoted"). A line with no req quote fails. The status stays "awaiting manager accept" until a person marks each line accepted; a req with zero usable lines is a valid result and prints "lines: 0/0".
scorecard.forbidden: Adding a trait the req does not state (culture fit, energy, leadership presence). The req wins; drop the line.
scorecard.gate: ABSENT accept (the hiring manager accepts each scorecard line; the draft is prepared with req quotes and stops at status "awaiting manager accept")

extract.trigger: An accepted scorecard and a resume are both present and the ask is to fill the scorecard fields. Quiet when the scorecard is not yet accepted.
extract.doneWhen: `jq` (with the resume loaded via --rawfile and split into lines) validates the output: keys equal the accepted scorecard fields exactly, and each value is null or an object with a value, a quote string and a resume line number where the quote is a substring of that resume line. An extra key, a missing key, or a quote that does not resolve at its line fails; a null field passes. An all-null result is valid.
extract.forbidden: Inferring a trait or filling a blank from tone, school, or fluency. A field without a quoted resume line stays null.

screen-note.trigger: An accepted scorecard and one candidate's extracted fields or resume are present, and the ask is a note per line. Quiet when asked for an overall score.
screen-note.doneWhen: `jq` (with the resume loaded via --rawfile and split into lines) counts notes: the number of notes equals the number of scorecard lines (N/N), each note is null or a quote with a locator whose quote is a substring of that resume line, and no overall, vibe, or total field exists in the output. An unsupported line stays blank and passes; a missing or extra note, an unresolved quote, or any overall field fails.
screen-note.forbidden: Adding an overall vibe score, summary rating, or recommendation field. One note per line, nothing aggregated.

compare.trigger: Two or more candidates' screen notes share one accepted scorecard. Quiet for a single candidate or when lines differ between candidates.
compare.doneWhen: `jq` joins the grid to each candidate's screen notes by scorecard line and compares: for every candidate and every line, the grid cell equals that candidate's screen-note value for that line (a null note gives a null cell; a cell filled where the note is null, or a value taken from another line, fails). Each candidate has exactly N cells for N lines, and no rank, total, or fluency field exists. A null cell stays null and passes; exit code 0 on all-match.
compare.forbidden: Ranking or scoring candidates on writing polish or fluency, or filling a missing cell from another line. Missing stays missing.
absentTools: blind-review redaction tool for style normalization

decide.trigger: A compare grid exists and the ask is to decide, pick, or hire. Prepare the sheet and stop; a person hires.
decide.doneWhen: A person reads the sheet and decides. No program can pass a hire. The sheet lists the compare grid cells as quoted evidence, nulls as missing, and ends with the line "STOP: a human decides."
decide.forbidden: Naming a winner, drafting an offer, or sending anything. The hire tool is absent; a reminder is not a gate.
decide.gate: ABSENT hire, offer, send (prepare the decision sheet from the compare grid, stop; a human decides and hires)

education.now: explain assisted to reliable; curriculum gated to a person

explain.trigger: A learner names one concept and wants it explained. Quiet when two or more concepts are named, or when the ask is to mark, drill, or plan a course.
explain.doneWhen: Before writing, the one concept's neighbouring terms are saved to neighbours.txt (model-authored today, so the term search is only as strong as that list). The reply is exactly three non-empty lines, one each starting 'Concept:', 'Example:', 'Question:' (count 1/1/1), no body text, and the last starts with 'Question:' and ends with '?'. leaks = (non-empty lines outside those three) + (neighbours.txt terms found anywhere in the reply other than the Concept line); leaks must be 0. 'Concept not stated' is a valid result.
explain.forbidden: Leaking a second concept: naming, defining, or previewing a neighbouring idea in the Example, the Question, or any extra line.
absentTools: concept-graph or glossary service (supplies the neighbouring terms so neighbours.txt is not model-authored)

check.trigger: A learner answer exists for a restate or one-application prompt, with the key written down first, and the last answer was a miss. Quiet when no key exists, or when the ask is many questions on one skill.
check.doneWhen: After a miss, the old and new example are saved to old_example.txt and new_example.txt, each starting with a 'scenario:' line, and python3 compares their lowercase word sets: Jaccard similarity must be below 0.5 (exit 0 pass, exit 1 means the paragraph or scenario was repeated or reworded and fails). A hit needs no new example, so no comparison run is a valid result.
check.forbidden: Repeating the same paragraph or the same scenario after a miss; rewording or a one-byte edit does not count, the scenario must change.
absentTools: scenario-similarity checker (a program under desk/ that exits 1 when two examples overlap too much)

sequence.trigger: A learner's current state is given (a quiz result, a stated stuck point) and the ask is what comes next. Quiet when the ask is for the whole path or an order of topics.
sequence.doneWhen: The whole reply is exactly two non-empty lines: one starting 'gap:' and one starting 'next:' (count 1/1, total non-empty lines 2), each at most 160 characters, and the 'next:' line contains no ';', no numerals-with-period or bullet markers, and none of 'then', 'after that', 'finally', 'step 2' (so prose course dumps fail). 'gap: none found' with 'next: none' is valid when evidence shows no gap; no stated state gives 'gap: unsupported'.
sequence.forbidden: Laying out the whole course: any list of steps beyond the single next one.
absentTools: learner-record store (would make the smallest-gap judgment a lookup)

drill.trigger: One named skill and an answer key (or a computable answer) exist. Quiet when the key is absent, or when the ask spans more than one skill.
drill.doneWhen: A python3 script marks every given answer against the stored key file and prints one 'marked: N/N' line with each mark citing a key item locator; exit 0 only when N equals the number of answers given and every answer has a key item. No key prints 'marked: 0/N unmarked, key absent' and is valid.
drill.forbidden: Moving on inside the same directive: any text after the marked line that introduces a second skill, a next level, or a new item set, or marking an answer with no key.
absentTools: key-marking script under desk/ (not yet written)

curriculum.trigger: A request to order topics, plan a course, or set a curriculum. Quiet for one concept, one check, or one next step.
curriculum.doneWhen: A person reads the proposal and sets the order. The proposal file is marked 'status: proposed' and no 'order set' field is written by the model.
curriculum.forbidden: Running an autonomous curriculum: fixing the order, presenting it as final, or starting lessons from it before a person sets it.
curriculum.gate: ABSENT accept (prepare the proposed order, stop; a person sets it)

personal-admin.now: triage reliable on headers plus a rule; send, book, and pay denied

triage.trigger: A mailbox or thread list is present and a triage rule is stated; quiet when no rule exists or the ask is to reply.
triage.doneWhen: One program reads the triage log and the header list and compares id sets: the opened thread ids equal the rule-marked header ids (symmetric difference 0), printed "opened: N/N"; exits 0 only then. 0/0 is valid.
triage.forbidden: Opening a thread the rule did not mark, opening before the header scan, or replying while triaging.

draft.trigger: Exactly one thread id is named and a reply is wanted; quiet for send or multiple threads.
draft.doneWhen: Program greps the draft's quoted ask line in the named thread's message text at the cited message locator (quote: msg N, line L); exits 0 only if the quote is verbatim there. No thread or no ask yields "no draft: unsupported", which is valid. Stop-before-send is enforced by the absent send, reply, forward tools and the deny hook, not by this check: the output is draft text only.
draft.forbidden: Sending, replying, or forwarding the draft, or answering a question the thread never asked.
draft.gate: ABSENT send, reply, forward (prepare the draft text and stop; a person sends)

brief.trigger: Calendar events with start and end times for a stated window are present; quiet when only prose exists.
brief.doneWhen: Program computes every pair of calendar events with startA < endB and startB < endA from the structured times and prints the list (overlaps: N/N); the brief's list equals that list and names both events of each pair. Back-to-back (endA == startB) is excluded. 0/0 is valid. No calendar times means unread.
brief.forbidden: Calling a back-to-back or near-miss a conflict, or naming an overlap from prose without calendar times.

pack.trigger: A meeting and source threads or documents are present; quiet when no source is attached.
pack.doneWhen: Program greps each item's verbatim quote at its cited locator in that item's own source and prints "items: N/N sourced"; exits 0 only if every kept item greps. Unsourced items are dropped; an empty agenda (0/0) is valid.
pack.forbidden: Adding an agenda item from memory alone, two items from one source, or paraphrasing a source into a quote it does not contain.

book.trigger: A booking is wanted (travel, appointment, reservation, event); always gated, prepare details and stop.
book.doneWhen: Bash:jq -e exits 0 on the booking sheet JSON: non-empty what, who, when, where, price, source_link and booked false. Stop is enforced by the absent book tools (calendar create_event, Zapier or other write actions, form or browser submit), not by this check.
book.forbidden: Creating the event or reservation, submitting a booking form, or reporting a booking as done.
book.gate: ABSENT book, calendar create_event, zapier write action, form or browser submit (prepare the booking sheet, stop; a person books)

pay.trigger: A payment is wanted (bill, invoice, fee, purchase); always gated, prepare details and stop.
pay.doneWhen: Bash:jq -e exits 0 on the payment sheet JSON: non-empty payee, amount, due_date, source_document and paid false. Stop is enforced by the absent pay, payment, checkout tools, not by this check.
pay.forbidden: Submitting a payment, entering card or account numbers, checking out, or reporting a payment as made.
pay.gate: ABSENT pay, payment, checkout, form or browser submit (prepare the payment sheet, stop; a person pays)

computer-use.now: ceiling not awarded; OSWorld numbers conflict; file memory works, transcript memory does not

perceive.trigger: A screenshot file and a named target (button, field, tab, dialog) are present and the question is whether the target is visible and unobstructed. Quiet when no screenshot exists or when the ask is to click.
perceive.doneWhen: Output names the target, quotes the screenshot path with a pixel bounding box (path:x,y,w,h), and prints occluded: yes|no naming any covering modal. 'target absent' and 'occluded: yes' are valid passing results; a remembered coordinate with no screenshot locator fails.
perceive.forbidden: Clicking or reporting a remembered location instead of the one in this screenshot, or calling a target visible when a modal covers it.

plan.trigger: An external step list file (steps.md), an executed-steps log (done.txt, one executed line number per line, empty if none), and a current screenshot or screen description are all present. Quiet when no list exists; ask for one instead of inventing steps.
plan.doneWhen: Output is exactly one action quoted verbatim from one line of steps.md with its line number (steps.md:L7), and L7 must be the next unexecuted step: the lowest non-blank line number of steps.md that is absent from done.txt. A python3 one-liner computes that line number and string-compares the quote; exit 0 only on exact match, so a skipped or reordered step fails. If the screen disagrees with that next step, output ASK with a one-line disagreement and no action. Two actions or an action not in the list fails.
plan.forbidden: Diverging from the step list: inventing, merging, skipping, or reordering steps (picking any line other than the next unexecuted one), or guessing when the screen and list disagree instead of asking.

act.trigger: One approved action has been performed by the host's approved GUI driver (not by this skill), and pre-state.json and post-state.json both exist. Quiet when the action is not yet chosen or no pre-state was captured.
act.doneWhen: python3 loads pre-state.json and post-state.json and prints each changed field as field: before -> after. Pass only if the printed diff is exactly the one expected change (field plus before and after values). An empty diff or any extra changed field fails; a click returning success is not a result. If post-state.json is missing the result is 'unread', not pass.
act.forbidden: Reporting success because the click or keystroke ran, with no after-state diff; or performing the click or keystroke from this skill, which holds no act tool.

recover.trigger: A step produced an unexpected state diff, a saved pre-step snapshot exists, and a revert has been carried out by a person or the host's approved GUI driver. Quiet when no snapshot was saved: report that revert cannot be confirmed.
recover.doneWhen: Output first prints 'bad step: <step id or steps.md:L<n>>' naming the step that caused the unexpected diff; without that line the result fails. After the revert is made by a person or host driver (this skill holds no act tool), `cmp pre-step-snapshot post-revert-snapshot` exits 0; then stop with no further action. Non-zero cmp is reported as 'revert unconfirmed' and also stops. The check is the cmp exit code.
recover.forbidden: Continuing or retrying the task after the revert, claiming a revert without confirming the prior state, or reverting from this skill instead of naming the step and stopping.

remember.trigger: A fact observed at one step is needed at a later step. Quiet when the next step uses it directly.
remember.doneWhen: Write the fact to state.json; at the later step `jq -e '.<key> == "<value>"' state.json` exits 0 and the value matches the quoted source. A missing key exits non-zero and is reported 'unread', a valid result.
remember.forbidden: Relying on the transcript to recall the fact at the later step instead of reading state.json.

finish.trigger: The last step list item is done and a submit control is the only remaining action. Quiet before then.
finish.doneWhen: Prepare only: list each instruction-required field with its final-state value from final-state.json and print 'unmet: 0' or 'unmet: <field>' per mismatched or unread field, then stop. Submit is performed by a person; it is never performed here. Early submit fails the card. Ceiling not awarded.
finish.forbidden: Submitting early, before the final state is checked field by field against the instruction; or submitting at all.
finish.gate: ABSENT submit (prepare the field-by-field unmet list, stop; a person presses submit)

strategy.now: compress reliable; analogy's does-not-transfer half is the weak part

compress.trigger: A source document and a request to compress it to assumptions and kill conditions. Quiet when the ask is a general summary, a rewrite, or a framing task.
compress.doneWhen: `python3` over the output and the input prints "assumptions: A", "kill: K" and "other: 0". A and K count lines starting "A:" and "K:"; other counts every non-blank line that starts with neither, and any other > 0 exits 1 (the rest must be cut). Each A:/K: line carries a locator (source line or section) and a quote that appears verbatim in the input. An input that states no assumption or no kill condition is a valid result: write "assumptions: 0" or "kill: 0" and do not invent one. Exit 0 only if other is 0 and every quote matches the input.
compress.forbidden: Keeping a line that is neither a stated assumption nor a kill condition, or inventing an unstated assumption. An assumption not stated does not exist.

frame.trigger: A problem is given and the ask is to frame it. Quiet when the ask is to rank options, summarise, or pick one statement.
frame.doneWhen: `python3` over the output prints "statements: 2" and "actions: 2 distinct": exactly two lines starting "P:" each followed by one line starting "Action:". After lowercasing and removing stop words, the two Action lines must have different leading verbs and a content-word overlap (Jaccard) of at most 0.34, and the two P: lines must also overlap at most 0.6; otherwise it prints "restatement" and exits 1. Exit 0 only then. A source with only one framing is a valid result: print "statements: 1" and exit 1 rather than pad a restatement. The program only rejects near-restatements; whether the actions differ in practice stays a person review.
frame.forbidden: Writing a restatement: a second statement whose Action line matches the first in substance. Drop it.

analogy.trigger: A proposed analogy or a request to reason by analogy. Quiet when no source domain is named or the ask is a rank or a what-if.
analogy.doneWhen: `python3` over the output prints "analogy: 3/3" only if exactly three labelled non-empty lines exist: "Source:", "Transfers:", "Does not transfer:", and no later line (any reasoning after the three) contains a content word that appears in the Does not transfer line but not in the Transfers line; a hit prints "analogy: leak <word>" and exits 1. A line reading "Does not transfer: none found" prints "analogy: 2/3 (none stated)" and exits 1: the skipped half is flagged, not smoothed. Whether the Does not transfer line is true stays a person review.
analogy.forbidden: Skipping or softening the Does not transfer line, or using a property from it afterwards.

constrain.trigger: A closed list of options plus a time and money budget. Quiet when the options are not yet listed or the ask is to generate more.
constrain.doneWhen: `python3` compares the output to the input option list and prints "rank: N/N" and "new: 0". Each option has a "time:" and "money:" value, the order is ascending by time then money, and a line starting "Runner-up lost:" names the second option with a reason quoting its time or money. Exit 0 only if every ranked name is in the input list (a name outside the list prints "new: 1" and exits 1). A list with fewer than two options prints "rank: 1/1" with no runner-up and is valid.
constrain.forbidden: Adding a new idea: any option in the ranking that was not in the input list.

what-if.trigger: A decision with named variables and a request to test a change. Quiet when more than one variable is to move or no decision exists.
what-if.doneWhen: `python3` over the base and moved tables counts rows marked "moved". If the output states "Binding: none" (the request moves no single variable, an unsupported case) and no row is marked moved, it prints "binding: none named" and exits 0 (valid result, no move is made). Otherwise it prints "moved: 1" and "held: H" where H equals the count of other variables in the base case, and every held cell equals its base value, and exits 0 only if exactly one row is moved and a "Decision:" line appears for base and moved cases. A second moved variable prints "moved: 2" and exits 1; a held cell that differs from base prints "held: drift" and exits 1.
what-if.forbidden: Drifting: changing a second variable, or a held value, while showing the moved case.

clinical-notes.now: documentation only; no diagnosis, no plan of care; the clinician signs

transcribe.trigger: A transcript and a note template are both present; fill the template fields from what was said. Quiet for diagnosis or plan of care.
transcribe.doneWhen: Every non-MISSING field value is a verbatim substring of the transcript, reported with its turn or line locator and checked by a program; a field the transcript does not state reads the literal MISSING. All-MISSING is a valid result.
transcribe.forbidden: Smoothing a gap into a finding: writing a plausible value, normal exam, or inferred symptom into a field the transcript does not state.

gap.trigger: A drafted note has empty or MISSING template fields; ask the clinician for exactly those fields.
gap.doneWhen: A program lists the MISSING or empty template fields by name and counts them; the set of field names in the ask equals that list (set equality by template field name, so every empty field is named and no filled field is named in its place), with no proposed value. Zero gaps is valid: output reads gaps: 0.
gap.forbidden: Inventing the field: filling an empty field with a guessed value, suggesting an answer, or asking about a filled field.

cite.trigger: A drafted note and its source transcript are present; trace each line to the transcript and cut lines it does not hold.
cite.doneWhen: Each kept line is followed by a quote that is a verbatim substring of the transcript with a turn or line locator, checked by a program; unmatched lines are cut and listed. All cut or empty transcript is valid: kept 0, cut N.
cite.forbidden: Importing history: keeping a line from the chart, a prior visit, or medical knowledge that was not spoken in this transcript.

sign.trigger: A note has passed transcribe, gap, and cite and awaits the clinician; present it and stop.
sign.doneWhen: A program diffs the presented note against the note that passed cite: the only difference is an empty signature block. Any added assessment, impression, plan of care, agent-written signature, attestation, or signed date fails the diff. Presenting the cite-passed note unchanged with an empty signature block is the valid result. Only the clinician signs, outside this session.
sign.forbidden: Becoming a diagnosis: adding an assessment, impression, or plan of care, or marking the note signed, approved, or final on the clinician's behalf.
sign.gate: ABSENT sign, diagnose (present the note, stop; the clinician signs)

security-review.now: defensive only; scan is tool stdout; no exploit skill

scan.trigger: A repo or branch is present and the ask is to scan for leaked secrets; defensive only.
scan.doneWhen: One result line from one tool run: mcp__github__run_secret_scanning stdout quoted verbatim with exit status; each finding a quoted tool line with file and line; zero findings valid as 'secret scan: 0 findings'; a scan that did not run is 'secret scan: unscanned'; a finding without a quoted scanner line is never reported and unscanned is never reported as clean.
scan.forbidden: Reporting a model hunch as a finding: anything not a quoted line of scanner output.

diff.trigger: A diff or scanner finding is present and the ask is file, line, and what it reaches; stop there.
diff.doneWhen: Each item is a quoted line with file:line from git diff output, one sentence of reach, then STOP; no reproduction steps; zero items valid as 'diff: 0 items'; unquotable lines dropped.
diff.forbidden: Continuing past the reach sentence into payload text, exploit steps, or a proof of concept.
absentTools: harness stop hook that blocks attack continuation

rank.trigger: Quoted findings and a written rubric are both present and the ask is to order them.
rank.doneWhen: Precondition: no written rubric gives 'rank: unsupported' and empty input gives 'rank: 0 rows', before any row. Rubric file lines are 'clause | pattern | rank'. Check: for every ranked row, one python3 -c run exits 0 only when the quoted text is a substring of line <line> of <file> and the row's cited clause exists in the rubric with its pattern inside the quote and its rank equal to the row's rank; a row that exits non-zero (including a rank that ignores or contradicts its clause) is removed as dropped; rows in equal rows out plus dropped, both stated.
rank.forbidden: Ranking unquoted code: assigning severity to anything no quoted line supports.

patch-review.trigger: A quoted finding and a proposed patch are both present and the ask is whether the quoted line changed.
patch-review.doneWhen: git diff -U0 base..head -- file read against the quoted file:line gives exactly one verdict: 'changed: old -> new' with the @@ hunk locator when a hunk covers that line and its '-' line equals the quote; 'unchanged: line at file:line' when no hunk covers it (empty diff included); 'unmatched' when the base line at file:line is not the quote.
patch-review.forbidden: Opening, filing, or drafting the fix task, issue, or pull request (the human hand-off dropping out), or declaring the vulnerability fixed from a plausible patch without a diff hunk touching the quoted line.

harness.now: skill and hook reliable; trace weak without a tool property; the agent does not promote itself

skill.trigger: A SKILL.md is being authored or its description tuned. One trigger, one trick. Quiet for hook, memory, trace, evolve asks.
skill.doneWhen: A static lint over the SKILL.md (python3; the wrong-task fire test is a separate model-judged check and is not part of this exit code) exits 0 only if: the description has exactly one 'Use when' clause; the description and the Trigger section each contain 'Quiet' followed by a stated quiet case; the Done-when section has exactly one 'check:' line and exactly one backticked command, and the Tool section exactly one 'tool:' line (one trick). A missing or empty file is unsupported, not a pass.
skill.forbidden: Firing on the wrong task: two triggers, a broad description, or no stated quiet case. Writing a second trick (a second check command or tool) into the same file instead of a second skill.

hook.trigger: A lifecycle event (PreToolUse, PostToolUse, Stop) needs a blocking check. Quiet for reminders or prose.
hook.doneWhen: python3 .claude/hooks/test_hooks.py exits 0 (git ls-files .claude/hooks/test_hooks.py lists it): the hook exits 2 on a case where the model would have continued, exits 0 on a clean case. A hook that never fired fails.
hook.forbidden: Exit 1 or 0 on a bad condition, or warning and letting the model continue; only exit 2 blocks.

memory.trigger: A note must be saved or recalled during a coding task, keyed by stage analyze, reproduce, edit, verify. Quiet for story-like summaries of a past session.
memory.doneWhen: Recall is a stage filter, jq -c --arg s STAGE 'select(.stage==$s)' memory.jsonl, saved to recalled.jsonl; jq -s -e --arg s STAGE '($s|IN("analyze","reproduce","edit","verify")) and all(.[]; .stage==$s and (.body|type=="string" and length<=280 and (contains("\n")|not)))' recalled.jsonl exits 0: STAGE is one of analyze, reproduce, edit, verify; every recalled record carries exactly the requested stage (a record recalled by similar story fails); every body is a string of at most 280 characters with no newline (longer or multi-line bodies are episode blobs and fail). Zero recalled records is valid.
memory.forbidden: Storing an episode blob, or retrieving by similar story instead of by stage.
absentTools: stage-keyed memory store with retrieval api

trace.trigger: A log of agent actions is kept as a record of what happened and must be append-only.
trace.doneWhen: python3 .claude/hooks/test_hooks.py deny exits 0, running desk/gate.py through the PreToolUse hook: a Write to trace/trace.jsonl, a Bash rm, a truncating redirect and a sed -i on it each exit 2, while cat, tail and python3 desk/desk.py verify-trace exit 0 (attempts to tamper or delete fail). Detection of a mid-file edit is the separate python3 desk/desk.py verify-trace, which exits 1 naming the line. Not covered: tail edit, truncation and a write by a route the patterns miss; real append-only needs chattr +a or a remote write-once sink, both absent.
trace.forbidden: Giving the agent a write or delete path to its own trace, or trusting its report that the log is intact.
trace.gate: ABSENT write, delete (the agent holds no write or delete path to its own trace: the PreToolUse hook denies them; a person or an external sink owns the file)

evolve.trigger: One harness piece was changed and a baseline exists; decide promotion on a held-out task with token count.
evolve.doneWhen: test "$(git diff --name-only BASE CAND -- .claude CLAUDE.md | wc -l)" -eq 1 && python3 desk/desk.py promote-gate <json> exits 0 printing PROMOTE: exactly one harness file differs between baseline and candidate (two files is two evolve runs), candidate.heldout_pass and candidate.tune_pass are true and candidate.tokens is less than baseline.tokens, both counts present in the json and published with the result; a json lacking either token count is unsupported, not PROMOTE. HOLD (exit 1) is valid. A person promotes.
evolve.forbidden: Promoting on a tuning-set gain only, or the agent promoting its own change.
evolve.gate: ABSENT promote (prepare change, held-out result and token count, stop; a person promotes)
absentTools: held-out benchmark runner with token meter

reverse-engineering.now: interoperability and defensive understanding only; deterministic tools first; no decryption, no bypass

triage.trigger: One or more files are in hand and the ask is what is this: format, class, endianness, architecture, entry. Quiet for function lists, call graphs, naming, lifting, or decrypting or bypassing anything.
triage.doneWhen: `python3 fixtures/re-triage/check.py --fixture <dir> --out <out.json>` exits 0: for each file the output fields format, class, endian, arch, and entry (the entry point address) equal what the checker parses from `file` and `readelf -h` itself, or is {"stop":"tools disagree"} when the tools error or disagree, or {"unsupported":"not ELF"}.
triage.forbidden: any field the tools did not emit; continuing past a disagreement; anything beyond identification (no decryption, no bypass)

static.trigger: A binary is in hand and triage already named its format and architecture; the ask is the function list, call graph, or strings. Quiet for names or purposes, runtime behavior, or decrypting or bypassing.
static.doneWhen: One combined output holding the function list, the call-graph edge list, and the strings is generated from `objdump -d` and `strings` output twice, and `cmp first.out second.out` exits 0 (all three regenerate byte for byte). A binary with no functions is a valid result: empty function and edge sections that regenerate empty, not a guess.
static.forbidden: redrawing or editing the call graph by hand or by model; adding an edge or function the disassembler output does not show; listing any function address or string the tool output does not contain
absentTools: headless disassembler with a call-graph export

lift.trigger: A known-architecture sample with ground truth exists and a target needs a recovered spec. Quiet when no scored sample exists, or for decrypting or bypassing.
lift.doneWhen: A scoring program run on the known-architecture sample prints the line "lift: M/N matched" and exits 0, and writes remainder.json holding exactly N-M items (the unmatched ones; `jq length remainder.json` equals N-M), which is the only input a model pass receives. M=N (empty remainder), or an unknown architecture reported as "unsupported", is a valid result.
lift.forbidden: sending the whole target, or any item outside remainder.json, to a model; touching the target before the known-architecture score exists; calling an unknown-ISA lift reliable

dynamic.trigger: A static claim list and a saved emulation trace are both in hand. Quiet when only one exists, to start hardware, or to decrypt or bypass anything.
dynamic.doneWhen: A comparison program prints "claims: K kept, D dropped of N" with K+D=N; each dropped claim cites the contradicting trace line by line number and no kept claim has one. With no trace the result is "unsupported: no trace" and exit 0.
dynamic.forbidden: keeping a claim the trace contradicts, or dropping one without a cited trace line; inventing a trace when no emulator is registered

protocol.trigger: Saved captures are in hand and the ask is to parse them and show the parse reproduces them. Quiet for live interception, crafting or replaying traffic, or decrypting or bypassing.
protocol.doneWhen: For every capture, parse then re-serialize, and `cmp capture.bin roundtrip.bin` exits 0. A capture that does not round-trip is reported as failed, and an empty capture set is a valid result.
protocol.forbidden: parsing any field not seen in the captures in hand; generalizing a field layout, length rule, or message type past the captures in hand; calling a spec from a few captures trustworthy

summarize.trigger: A function from disassembly or decompilation needs a name or one-line purpose. Quiet when the ask is only listing functions, or decrypting or bypassing anything.
summarize.doneWhen: Each proposed name carries a quoted evidence line: a string with its offset, a call target with its address, or a trace line with its line number, confirmed by a program to appear in the tool output at that locator. A function with no evidence stays unnamed, a valid result. This proves the evidence exists, not that the name is right.
summarize.forbidden: giving a plausible name with no string, call, or trace behind it

state.trigger: Findings from any reverse-engineering directive exist, or a session must resume one. Quiet when there is nothing yet to record.
state.doneWhen: A fresh session reads only the state file and its listed artifacts and writes restated.json; then `jq -S .findings state.json > a.json; jq -S .findings restated.json > b.json; cmp a.json b.json` exits 0 (the resumed findings equal the saved findings). An empty findings list is a valid result.
state.forbidden: leaving findings in chat only, or resuming from memory instead of the files
